headline: High-risk default filesystem and network exposure in Langflow can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a read-only content writer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and arbitrary HTTP/model outputs, and its server-side flows can chain agents; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself ingest outputs. The pair creates a plausible shared-file or flow-output bridge, but not a documented automatic channel, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Langflow flow nodes read attacker-controlled files or HTTP responses as instructions
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Disable file-based instruction parsing in Langflow flows
Add provenance labels to all flow inputs and outputs
Use a separate workspace for any content passed to python-cheatsheet
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer node before any LLM prompt
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted templates for agent handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow reads the server filesystem and uploaded files, and it can call arbitrary HTTP/model providers; python-cheatsheet is local documentation-only with no file access. If sensitive flow inputs are routed into Langflow, outputs or prompts can leak through configured providers, but the second agent does not independently expand the leak surface.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into Langflow flows
IF Langflow components send those contents to external model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Restrict Langflow to non-sensitive test data
Turn off external provider nodes for sensitive flows
Store secrets outside flow inputs
Review uploaded-file handling before execution
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress; python-cheatsheet is non-runnable and write-free. The conflict is one-sided in practice, but Langflow's default server-side writes can still collide with shared files or stores if the pair is deployed together, and uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or shared store
IF Langflow flow execution writes artifacts while another process edits the same path
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Mount python-cheatsheet read-only
Disable concurrent writes in Langflow deployments
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: isolate Langflow state per flow run

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative downstream; python-cheatsheet is a reference artifact that may be copied into prompts or docs. There is no evidence of autonomous action-taking by the second agent, so the cascade is real but bounded to medium.
conditions: IF Langflow output is copied into a downstream prompt without verification
IF a flow node uses generated text as a factual source for another step
mitigations: Require human review before reusing generated text
Add citation checks between flow stages
Mark generated outputs as untrusted by default
Use a verification node before any action step
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments stated. Langflow handles flow inputs and stored secrets, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so only a small compliance gap is plausible and only if sensitive data is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Langflow flows
IF deployment policy requires retention or residency controls not configured in Langflow
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in these agents
Document retention settings for Langflow stores
Keep secrets out of flow inputs
Review deployment region settings
requires-engineering: add compliance logging and deletion workflows
